{"file_path":"~/.claude/plans/pasted-content-id-bba5-we-are-transient-nautilus.md","content":"# Coordinated views: one focus, one filter, one URL

## Context

The UI shows the zoom tree on the left and graph, timeline and search as tabs on the right.
They share only a `selected` node id, so they feel like separate tools: the timeline can't
filter the graph, zooming the graph doesn't show up in the timeline, and search always covers
the whole session with no kind filters. Only one tab is visible at a time, so no linking
could be seen anyway.

The goal is coordinated views: every view is a projection of one shared viewer state, and
that state is the URL. Decisions from the user:

- **Layout:** timeline as a scrubber strip on top, filter bar above it, zoom tree left, graph right, all visible at once.
- **Graph zoom is semantic:** focusing a phase re-roots the graph to its turns, focusing a turn shows its steps. No pixel pan or zoom.
- **Scope hierarchy:** project is the root. "Go into" a session pins it as root, so reset and Esc never throw the user out of the session they are working in.
- **New design principle, addressability:** the URL is a deep link to the full viewer state, shareable and bookmarkable, and as short as possible.

## Challenges to the original ideas (folded into the design)

- **Separate focus from filter.** Focus narrows what every view shows (a node or a time window). Filter and query only highlight and dim, inside the focus. Mixing them would make "show only tool errors" hide the context needed to understand them.
- **Separate select from focus.** Single click selects: the item is highlighted in all views and scrolled into the reader. Double click or Enter focuses. Hover previews across views.
- **Hits belong in context, not only in a list.** Matches show as ticks on the timeline, counts on tree rows and accented graph nodes. The results list becomes a toggle in the reader pane.
- **Empty query plus a filter is a feature.** "User prompts" with no text lists every prompt in scope, which is a table of contents for the session or project.
- **The timeline brush snaps to turn boundaries.** A free time range would cut turns in half and map to no node in the tree or graph.
- **Esc goes up one level, not to the top.** The reset button jumps to the pinned root.
- **Back and forward work.** Focus changes push history entries; typing and brushing replace the current one.

## Viewer state and URL

One `ViewState`, parsed from and written to the URL, drives everything:

| State | URL form | Default (omitted) |
|---|---|---|
| project | first path segment, the project name (`name~abcd` only if two names clash) | most recent project |
| pinned session | second path segment, session id prefix (shortest unique, min 6) | none: project root |
| focus node | third path segment, structure id (`p2`, `t7`, `t7.s3`) | pinned root |
| time window | `t=120-480`, seconds from focus start, snapped to turns | whole focus |
| selection | `x=t7.s3` | none |
| text query | `q=salt` | empty |
| filters | `k=u,t:Bash,e` (codes below) | none |
| granularity | `z=s` (t, a, s, f) | abstract |

Filter codes: `u` user prompts, `a` assistant text, `h` thinking, `t` tool calls, `t:Name`
calls to one tool, `e` tool errors, `s` subagent activity, `c` compactions and commands,
`r` rewound turns.

Example: `http://127.0.0.1:9656/yolo-twice/34b27c/p2?q=salt&k=t,e&x=t2.s3`

The path is the breadcrumb. The engine already serves the UI with an SPA fallback, so path
routes work on reload.

## Layout

```
┌ yolo-twice ▸ 34b27c ▸ phase 2 ▸ turn 7      [⤒ reset]  slider · catch me up · live ┐
│ 🔍 query…   [user] [assistant] [thinking] [tools ▾] [errors] [subagents] [rewinds] │
│ ▁▂▅█▃▁ ▁▂▇█▅▂▁ ▁▃▅▂   turns as bars, hit ticks, focus window shaded, brush        │
├──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Reader [outline | results (12)]  │ Graph of the focus node, re-rooted on focus      │
│ zoom tree rooted at the focus    │ hits accented, non-matches dimmed, selection     │
│ hit counts per row               │ ringed, double click focuses                     │
└──────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

At the project root the same layout shows sessions: the timeline has one bar per session on
a shared axis, the graph shows sessions in order, the reader lists sessions and expands them
lazily. Double clicking a session goes into it and pins it.

## Implementation

### Shared pure code (analyzers)

- `code/packages/analyzers/src/graph.ts`: generalize `toMermaid` to render any node: a session shows phases with their turns, a phase shows its turns with subagents, a turn shows its steps. Add `projectToMermaid(index)` for the project root. Node ids stay the structure ids, which the UI already maps back through pele's `data-id`.
- `code/packages/analyzers/src/search.ts`: store `agent_id` and `is_error` per document; extend `search()` options with `kinds`, `tools`, `from`, `to`; add a pure `filterEvents(events, filter)` used for empty queries and by the UI.

- `code/API.md`: document the parameters. `code/packages/ui/mock/server.ts` gets the same behaviour through the shared analyzers code.

### UI (`code/packages/ui/src`)

- New `state.ts`: `ViewState` type, `parseUrl` and `toUrl` with defaults omitted, a `useViewState` hook that pushes history on focus and session changes and

## Approved Plan:
# Coordinated views: one focus, one filter, one URL

## Context

The UI shows the zoom tree on the left and graph, timeline and search as tabs on the right.
They share only a `selected` node id, so they feel like separate tools: the timeline can't
filter the graph, zooming the graph doesn't show up in the timeline, and search always covers
the whole session with no kind filters. Only one tab is visible at a time, so no linking
could be seen anyway.

The goal is coordinated views: every view is a projection of one shared viewer state, and
that state is the URL. Decisions from the user:

- **Layout:** timeline as a scrubber strip on top, filter bar above it, zoom tree left, graph right, all visible at once.
- **Graph zoom is semantic:** focusing a phase re-roots the graph to its turns, focusing a turn shows its steps. No pixel pan or zoom.
- **Scope hierarchy:** project is the root. "Go into" a session pins it as root, so reset and Esc never throw the user out of the session they are working in.
- **New design principle, addressability:** the URL is a deep link to the full viewer state, shareable and bookmarkable, and as short as possible.

## Challenges to the original ideas (folded into the design)

- **Separate focus from filter.** Focus narrows what every view shows (a node or a time window). Filter and query only highlight and dim, inside the focus. Mixing them would make "show only tool errors" hide the context needed to understand them.
- **Separate select from focus.** Single click selects: the item is highlighted in all views and scrolled into the reader. Double click or Enter focuses. Hover previews across views.
- **Hits belong in context, not only in a list.** Matches show as ticks on the timeline, counts on tree rows and accented graph nodes. The results list becomes a toggle in the reader pane.
- **Empty query plus a filter is a feature.** "User prompts" with no text lists every prompt in scope, which is a table of contents for the session or project.
- **The timeline brush snaps to turn boundaries.** A free time range would cut turns in half and map to no node in the tree or graph.
- **Esc goes up one level, not to the top.** The reset button jumps to the pinned root.
- **Back and forward work.** Focus changes push history entries; typing and brushing replace the current one.

## Viewer state and URL

One `ViewState`, parsed from and written to the URL, drives everything:

| State | URL form | Default (omitted) |
|---|---|---|
| project | first path segment, the project name (`name~abcd` only if two names clash) | most recent project |
| pinned session | second path segment, session id prefix (shortest unique, min 6) | none: project root |
| focus node | third path segment, structure id (`p2`, `t7`, `t7.s3`) | pinned root |
| time window | `t=120-480`, seconds from focus start, snapped to turns | whole focus |
| selection | `x=t7.s3` | none |
| text query | `q=salt` | empty |
| filters | `k=u,t:Bash,e` (codes below) | none |
| granularity | `z=s` (t, a, s, f) | abstract |

Filter codes: `u` user prompts, `a` assistant text, `h` thinking, `t` tool calls, `t:Name`
calls to one tool, `e` tool errors, `s` subagent activity, `c` compactions and commands,
`r` rewound turns.

Example: `http://127.0.0.1:9656/yolo-twice/34b27c/p2?q=salt&k=t,e&x=t2.s3`

The path is the breadcrumb. The engine already serves the UI with an SPA fallback, so path
routes work on reload.

┌ yolo-twice ▸ 34b27c ▸ phase 2 ▸ turn 7      [⤒ reset]  slider · catch me up · live ┐
│ 🔍 query…   [user] [assistant] [thinking] [tools ▾] [errors] [subagents] [rewinds] │

## What yolo-twice does

- **Semantic zoom.** Read a session as one line, three sentences, a paragraph of phases, the
  turns, or the raw records. Any text, including the top summary and a long tool result, can be
  zoomed out one more step or expanded in place.
- **Live flow graph.** The conversation as a graph: turns, tool calls, subagents and rewind
  branches, updated while the session runs, merging into phases as you zoom out.
- **Attention slider.** From "micro management" (every turn summarized live) to "yolo"
  (nothing until you ask, then "catch me up"). You choose how many tokens and how much
  attention to spend; the cost is shown next to the slider.
- **Project-local history.** Everything derived lands in `.yolo-twice/` in your repo,
  redacted, plain JSON and mermaid, so you can commit it or gitignore it.
- **Incremental and idempotent.** Stop the engine, resume later, run it twice: same bytes.

## Install

data.description: Add principles and coordinated-views section to design doc, renumber

text:
{"command":"python3 -I - <<'EOF'
p='documentation/design.md'
s=open(p).read()
def rep(old,new):
    global s
    assert old in s, old[:70]; s=s.replace(old,new,1)

rep('### What exists and what we add','''### Design principles

- **Idempotency.** Every derived artifact is a pure function of its input and the analyzer
  version. Stop, resume, re-run, or run two writers at once: the bytes come out the same.
- **Addressability.** The URL is a deep link to the complete viewer state: project, session,
  focus, time window, selection, query, filters and text length. Any view can be bookmarked or
  pasted to a teammate and opens identically. URLs are as short as possible: defaults are
  omitted, ids are the shortest unique prefix.

### What exists and what we add''')

# renumber sections 7..12 -> 8..13 (from the end to avoid collisions)
for n in range(12, 6, -1):
    import re
    s=re.sub(rf'^## {n}\. ', f'## {n+1}. ', s, flags=re.M)

new_section='''## 7. Coordinated views and deep links

The UI shows four linked views at once: a filter bar, a timeline scrubber, the reader (the
zoom tree) and the graph. They are projections of one state, and that state is the URL.

- **Focus narrows.** The focus is a node: the project, a session, a phase, a turn or a step.
  The reader is rooted at it, the graph is redrawn one level below it (semantic zoom, no pixel
  zoom), and the timeline axis spans it. Double click focuses, Esc goes up one level, the
  breadcrumb jumps anywhere above.
- **The window narrows in time.** Dragging on the timeline sets a window that snaps to whole
  bars (turns, or steps inside a turn), so it always maps to nodes in the tree and graph.
- **Filter and query highlight, they never hide.** Matches inside the focus show as ticks on
  the timeline, counts on reader rows and accented graph nodes; everything else is dimmed. An
  empty query with a filter lists every match, for example all your prompts. Query and filter
  combine with AND; filter codes combine with OR.
- **Selection and hover link.** Click selects a node in every view; hover highlights it in
  every view.
- **Pinning.** The project is the root. Going into a session pins it, so reset and Esc stay in
  that session; unpinning returns to the project.

URL form:

```
/<project>/<session>/<focus>?t=<from>-<to>&x=<selected>&q=<query>&k=<filters>&z=<text length>
```

| Part | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `project` | project folder name, `name~abcd` only when two projects share a name | the engine's last project |
| `session` | shortest unique session id prefix, at least 6 characters; a leading `~` means not pinned | project root |
| `focus` | structure node id such as `p2`, `t7`, `t1.s5` | the session |
| `t` | window in seconds from the focus start, snapped to whole bars | whole focus |
| `x` | selected node | none |
| `q` | text query | none |
| `k` | filters: `u` your prompts, `a` assistant text, `h` thinking, `t` tool calls, `t:Name` one tool, `e` tool errors, `s` subagents, `c` compactions and commands, `r` rewound turns | none |
| `z` | default text length: `t` title, `a` abstract, `s` summary, `f` full | `a` |

Example: `http://127.0.0.1:9656/yolo-twice/34b27c/t2?k=t,e&x=t2.s4`

Filtering and search run in the browser over the loaded session events, so linking is
instant. At the project root the same filters go to the engine and search every session.

'''
rep('## 8. Plugin and install', new_section+'## 8. Plugin and install')

# idempotency rules: concurrent writers + normalizer version
rep('''1. Event identity is the record uuid. Re-ingesting the same line is a no-op.''','''1. Event identity is the record uuid. Re-ingesting the same line is a no-op, also when two
   writers (two engines, or an engine and `yolo-twice index`) run at once: ingestion of a
   session holds a lock in `cache/`, and the known-id set reloads when the file grows.''')
rep('''2. Each source file has a cursor.''','''2. Each source file has a cursor, and the cursor records the normalizer version. A new
   normalizer version rebuilds the session once.
   Each source file has a cursor.''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

Graph, timeline, search and the reader are now one linked workspace, with the whole view state in a short, shareable URL. 36 unit tests and 30 browser checks pass, and it works on this repo's live session. Everything is committed but not pushed.

**What changed in your ideas**

- **All views on one screen.** Tabs meant you could never see two views react at once. The filter bar and a timeline strip sit across the top, with the reader on the left and the graph on the right.
- **Focus and filter are separate.** Focus narrows every view to a node or time window. Query and filters only highlight inside the focus and dim the rest, so "errors" never hides the context around an error.
- **Zooming the graph is semantic.** Double-clicking a phase redraws the graph as its turns; Esc goes back up. The timeline and reader follow.
- **Brushing the timeline snaps to whole turns or steps.** A raw time range would cut turns in half and match nothing in the tree or graph.
- **Search is scoped to the focus.** Filters include your prompts, assistant text, thinking, tool calls, one specific tool, errors, subagents, compactions and rewinds. An empty query with a filter lists every match, for example all your prompts.
- **Project is the root; "go into" pins a session.** Reset and Esc then stay inside that session.
- **Addressability is now a design principle.** For example, this opens turn 2 with tool calls and errors highlighted:

```
http://127.0.0.1:9656/yolo-twice/34b27c/t2?k=t,e
```

**Bugs that real data exposed, now fixed**

- **Duplicated events.** Two engines writing the same project duplicated events in the committed index. My test engine running beside yours caused it, but a running engine plus `yolo-twice index` would too. Ingestion now takes a per-session lock, and reading skips duplicates.
- **Missing prompts.** Messages you send while Claude is working were dropped entirely, including "commit regularly" and "gh pages is active". They now appear inside the running turn.
- **Notifications counted as prompts.** Background task notifications were counted as your prompts. They are now system events.
- **Stale search after a rebuild.** After a session was rebuilt, search returned results from before the rebuild. The engine now rebuilds its search index whenever a session is reset.

I restarted your engine on port 9656 so it runs the new code. It rebuilt this repo's index once, now with no duplicates and 14 of your messages. Your browser tab reconnects on its own.

- Summaries without a Claude call show raw text with markup. That is the fallback I flagged last time.
- This whole session is one phase, because phases split only on compaction or a 30-minute idle gap.
- The header wraps to two lines when the breadcrumb is long.

Both are done: the merge conflict is analysed below, and follow mode is finished and verified. Nothing is committed yet, because a commit now would land inside your in-progress merge.

## The merge conflict

Only `.yolo-twice/project.json` conflicts. Everything else merged cleanly, including Roland's two new sessions.

- **Why it conflicts.** `project.json` is the only committed file that aggregates across sessions. It lists every session with its event count and last timestamp. Your engine rewrites it after every turn of the live session, and Roland's engine rewrote it to add his sessions. Two people indexing at the same time therefore always edit the same lines.
- **It is purely derived.** The file holds nothing that isn't in each session's own files. Your working copy already proves it: the running engine regenerated `project.json` during the merge, and the file now correctly lists all three sessions without conflict markers.
- **How to finish this merge.** Take the regenerated file as is:

```
git add .yolo-twice/project.json && git commit
```

## Avoiding it in the future

Splitting is the right instinct. The rule I'd adopt is **one writer per committed file**: every committed file belongs to exactly one session, and anything that combines sessions is rebuilt locally and never committed.

| File | Problem today | Proposal |
|---|---|---|
| `project.json` | shared aggregate, rewritten every turn | move to the gitignored `cache/`; rebuild from the sessions on start; add a small per-session `meta.json` so the project list stays cheap |
| `config.json` | your "micro" attention setting is committed for everyone | keep shared settings like redaction rules there; move attention to a gitignored per-user file |
| `sessions/<id>/source.json` | contains your absolute home path and byte cursors, churns every turn | gitignore it; without a cursor, ingestion re-reads and dedupes, so nothing is lost |
| `sessions/<id>/text/` | summaries of still-open nodes pile up, five versions of one abstract so far | write open-node summaries to `cache/`, commit only closed ones |
| `events.ndjson`, `structure.json`, `graph.mmd` | fine: one session, one writer | keep committed |

One risk remains. If two people continue the same session, for example via `resume`, both append to the same `events.ndjson`. Git's built-in union merge (`*.ndjson merge=union` in `.gitattributes`) would combine both sides' lines. Events then need sorting by timestamp when read, and the reader already drops duplicate ids. I haven't confirmed whether `claude --resume` keeps the session id, so this is worth checking before relying on it.

I haven't implemented any of this yet. Say the word and I'll do the split after you've concluded the merge.

## Follow mode

- **Turning it on.** The "follow" button, the `f` key or `End` keep the view on the newest events. The selection sits on the newest step, a focused turn jumps to the newest turn, and the reader scrolls the tail into view. It's part of the link, so `/yolo-twice?f` opens whichever session is active right now.
- **Turning it off.** It stops like a CI log does: click, brush, Esc or scroll up in the reader. A "2 new ↓" button then counts what arrived, and clicking it jumps back to the tail. Filters keep following, like `tail -f | grep`.
- **Bug fixed along the way.** The timeline and graph now mark the turn that contains a selected step, which they didn't before.
- **Verified.** 18 browser checks pass against an engine whose transcript was growing during the test. 39 unit tests pass, typecheck is clean, and there are no console errors.

## Context

`.yolo-twice/` is committed for team collaboration, but it carries machine-specific absolute
paths. Measured on the current folder (2.1 MB):

| What | Count | Where |
|---|---|---|
| project root `$PROJECT` | 296 | events, structure labels |
| home `~` (outside the project) | 65 | events |
| Claude folder slug `-~-…` | 120 | events (scratchpad and `~/.claude/projects` paths) |
| bare username `<user>` | 78 | events (`ls -la` owner columns and similar) |
| Roland's home `~` | 51 | his sessions, written by his engine |
| `origin_dir` absolute path | every `source.json` | |

Goals from the user: portability across the team, no disclosure of usernames or file-system
layout, fewer tokens. Constraint: Claude's tools need absolute paths, so `resume` must expand
them back. Decisions: the project root becomes `$PROJECT`, home becomes `~`, and the bare
username becomes `<user>`.

Token savings are honest but modest: about 10k characters, roughly 0.5% of the folder. The
real gains are privacy and portability.

Also verified for the resume question raised earlier. The Claude Code CLI reference says
`--resume` reuses the original session id unless `--fork-session` is passed, and that
`--resume` accepts an absolute path to a `.jsonl` transcript. Today's `yolo-twice resume`
writes into `~/.claude/projects/` and resumes in place. A teammate continuing a committed
session therefore appends to the same `sessions/<id>/` folder and recreates merge conflicts.

## Approach

### 1. A path rule in the redaction step (core)

New `code/packages/core/src/anonymize.ts`, a pure function plus its inverse:

```
anonymizePaths(text, { root, home, user }) -> text
expandPaths(text, { root, home }) -> text
```

Rules, applied longest first so the project root wins over home:

1. The project root, matched on a path boundary → `$PROJECT` (`$PROJECT/code/x` → `$PROJECT/code/x`).
2. The project's Claude slug, from `projectSlug(root)` in `paths.ts` → `<project-slug>`.
3. The home directory → `~` (`~/.claude/settings.json` → `~/.claude/settings.json`).
4. The home slug prefix inside other Claude folder names (`-~-` → `-~-`).
5. The bare login name, whole word only, when it is at least 4 characters and not a common English word → `<user>`.
6. Any other home-like prefix `/home/<name>/`, `/Users/<name>/` or `C:\Users\<name>\` → `~/`. This covers histories that mention another machine's paths.

Only rules 1 and 3 are expanded on resume; the others never need to be.

`code/packages/core/src/ingest.ts`: `applyRedaction` runs secret redaction and then the path rule over the event text and, newly, every string inside `data`. Today `data` (tool descriptions, task summaries) bypasses secret redaction as well. Root comes from the project being ingested, home and login name from `os.homedir()` and `os.userInfo()`.

`code/packages/core/src/schema.ts`: add `redaction.paths: boolean` (default true) to the config, so a team can switch it off.

`code/packages/core/src/sources/claude-code.ts`: bump `NORMALIZER_VERSION` to 3. Every engine rebuilds its own sessions once after pulling. Sessions from other machines are left alone, because their source isn't present, and their owner's engine rewrites them on the next pull.

`source.json`: store `origin_dir` in the `~` form.

### 2. Resume expands and forks (engine)

`code/packages/engine/src/resume.ts`:

- `reconstructTranscript` applies `expandPaths` with the resumer's project root and home to every text and tool input. Tools see real absolute paths.
- `prepareResume` writes the rebuilt transcript to `.yolo-twice/cache/resume/<id>.jsonl` (gitignored), not into `~/.claude/projects/`.
- The command becomes `claude --resume <absolute path to that file> --fork-session`. Claude Code creates a new session id, so the continuation is a new session with its own folder, and no committed session ever gets a second writer.
- On first use, verify with the installed CLI that path-resume and `--fork-session` work together. If they don't, fall back to writing the transcript under a fresh UUID in `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/` and resuming that id; the effect is the same.

`code/packages/engine/src/cli.ts` and `code/plugin/commands/yolo-twice.md`: print and run the new command.

### 3. Docs

- `documentation/design.md`: a "paths" rule next to redaction in §5, and resume now forks.
- `README.md` "What lands in your repo": paths are written as `$PROJECT` and `~`.
- `code/API.md`: the resume command line.

## Not in this change

- Splitting `project.json` and moving `source.json` and open-node summaries to `cache/`, from the merge-conflict analysis. That is a separate change, waiting for the user's go.
- The open merge and the uncommitted follow-mode work: the merge must be concluded first. Then follow mode gets committed, and only then this change starts.

## Verification

- Unit (`bun test` in `code/`):
  - `anonymizePaths` on fixture strings for every rule, path-boundary cases (`~` untouched, `~/git/yolo-twice-old` not treated as the root), the username guard, and Windows and macOS forms.
  - Round trip: `expandPaths(anonymizePaths(x))` returns `x` for paths under the root and home.
  - Ingest: no absolute home path and no login name in `events.ndjson`, `structure.json` or `source.json`; strings inside `data` are scrubbed too; normalizer v3 triggers exactly one rebuild.
  - Resume: the rebuilt transcript contains the resumer's absolute paths, lives under `cache/resume/`, and the command includes `--fork-session`.
- Real data: after rebuilding this repo, a scan of `.yolo-twice/` finds no `~`, no `-~-` and no bare `<user>`. Report the before and after character counts.
- Resume end to end: run `claude -p --resume <file> --fork-session "reply with ok and the absolute path of README.md"`. Confirm it answers with the real absolute path and that a new session id appears.
- `bun run typecheck`, the browser suites (linked views, follow) still green.

`.yolo-twice/` is now portable and anonymous. A resumed session gets the paths of whoever resumes it, and it continues as a new session, so a committed session never gets a second writer. Everything is committed and nothing is pushed.

**Your Claude resume question**

The Claude Code docs say `claude --resume <id>` reuses the original session id unless `--fork-session` is passed, so the risk was real. A teammate resuming a committed session would have written into the same `sessions/<id>/` folder and recreated merge conflicts.

`yolo-twice resume` now works like this:
- It rebuilds the transcript into the gitignored `cache/resume/` and writes nothing into `~/.claude`.
- It runs `claude --resume <file> --fork-session`, which gives the continuation its own new session id.

I tested this with the real CLI. The resumed model quoted the teammate's own absolute path, every resume got a fresh session id, and the original session was never written. I deleted the test sessions this created in your Claude folder.

**What gets written now**

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `$PROJECT/code/x` | `$PROJECT/code/x` |
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | `~/.claude/settings.json` |
| `<project-slug>` | `<project-slug>` |
| other homes such as `~` and their folder names | `~` and `-~-` |
| your login name as a whole word | `<user>` |

On resume, `$PROJECT` and `~` are expanded back to that person's machine, because Claude's file tools need absolute paths. The other replacements are one-way. This applies to every string an event carries. Secret redaction now also covers a field it used to skip: tool descriptions and task summaries. `redaction.paths: false` in `config.json` switches path rewriting off.

**Result on this repo**

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `~` | 435 | 0 |
| `-~-` | 151 | 0 |
| bare `<user>` | 88 | 0 |
| Roland's paths in your session | 23 | 0 |
| size of your session | 2.25 MB | 2.21 MB |

The token saving is small, about 2%; privacy and portability are the real gains. 45 unit tests and 30 browser checks pass.

**Things to know**

- **Roland's two sessions still contain `~`.** Their source isn't on your machine. His engine rewrites them once he pulls and restarts it, because the normalizer version changed.
- **One mangled name remains.** A garbled shell error contains `e-matthi-git`. My whole-word guard skips names joined by hyphens, and I left it rather than loosen the guard.
- **I concluded your merge.** The approved plan put that first, so I committed it with the regenerated `project.json`, then committed follow mode separately.
- **I restarted your engine on port 9656 twice** so it would load the new code.
- **The `project.json` split from the conflict analysis is still not done.** It also covers moving `source.json` and open-node summaries to `cache/`. You can see why it matters: micro mode had written over 90 summary files for still-open nodes before this rebuild cleared them.

## 5. `.yolo-twice` layout and idempotency

```
.yolo-twice/
  config.json                    # schema version, attention, redaction rules, enabled analyzers
  cache/                         # interim summaries, temp (gitignored)
  sessions/<session-id>/
    source.json                  # origin path, agent, cursor {bytes, lines, size, mtime, head hash}
    events.ndjson                # redacted normalized events, append-only in arrival order
    structure.json               # L0 to L3 tree with available granularities per node
    graph.mmd                    # flow graph as mermaid text, rendered with pele everywhere
    text/<node>.<gran>.<hash>.json   # title / abstract / summary per node, keyed by input hash + analyzer version
    semantic/<input-hash>.json   # phase labels and cluster results
  project.json                   # L-1: session list and project digest
  annotations/                   # user notes, later
  .gitignore                     # cache/
```

Engine runtime state (`engine.json` with pid and port, `projects.json`, `engine.log`) lives in
`~/.yolo-twice/`, never in the repo.

```

## What lands in your repo

```
.yolo-twice/
  config.json                  attention level, redaction rules, enabled analyzers
  project.json                 session list and project digest
  sessions/<id>/
    events.ndjson              redacted, normalized events
    structure.json             the zoom tree
    graph.mmd                  the flow graph as mermaid
    text/                      titles, abstracts and summaries per node
  cache/, engine.json          gitignored
```

Raw transcripts stay in `~/.claude`. Only redacted events and derived data are written here.

**Files created**
- `code/packages/pele-markdown/` (package.json, tsconfig, `src/index.ts`, `test/plugin.test.ts`): markdown-it plugin turning ```mermaid fences into `<div class="pele"><svg…>` at build time via pele's synchronous `render`; render errors become `<pre class="pele-error">`. Exports `peleMarkdown` (default) and `renderMermaid`. 2 tests pass; `tsc -b` builds to `dist/`.
- `code/site/` (package.json, `.vitepress/config.ts`, `.vitepress/theme/{index.ts,custom.css}`, `index.md`, `how-it-works.md`, `attention.md`, `install.md`, `credits.md`, `.gitignore`): VitePress 1.6.4, `base: /yolo-twice/`, default theme, nav + sidebar, status banner, `--pele-*` mapped to `--vp-c-*`. All content taken from README/design.md.
- `code/pitch/` (package.json, `slides.md`, `components/Pele.vue`, `style.css`, `.gitignore`): 9-slide Slidev 53 deck with speaker notes and timings; every diagram goes through `<Pele text="…">` which calls pele `mount()` client side.
- `.github/workflows/pages.yml`: setup-bun, `bun install --frozen-lockfile` in `code/`, builds plugin + site + deck, assembles site + `pitch/`, upload-pages-artifact + deploy-pages.

1. **Slidev 53 needs Node 22+** (its Vite 8/rolldown calls `util.styleText` with values Node 20.12 rejects). Local Node is 20.12, so the pitch `build`/`dev`/`export` scripts run the CLI through `bun node_modules/@slidev/cli/bin/slidev.mjs …`; this works locally and in CI (setup-bun). Site and plugin build fine on Node 20.

**Files created** (all under `code/packages/ui/`, 15 files, no edits elsewhere)
- `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `index.html`
- `src/main.tsx`, `src/App.tsx` (state, routing by `?project=&session=`, SSE handling, session list for L-1), `src/Header.tsx` (project, session picker, live dot, attention slider + calls/h readout, Catch me up), `src/Zoom.tsx` (stretchtext tree, per-node zoom in/out over title/abstract/summary/full, lazy `POST .../text`, raw events at L3 with redaction badges, branch/subagent/error badges, phase boundary markers), `src/Graph.tsx` (pele flowchart renderer, click maps `data-id` back to structure ids, selection highlight), `src/Timeline.tsx` (SVG strip per phase, bars per turn, colour by rewind/subagent/tool-error, tooltip), `src/Search.tsx`, `src/useStream.ts` (EventSource with backoff), `src/api.ts` (typed client for every API.md endpoint, event pagination via `after`, helpers), `src/styles.css` (tokens on `:root`, dark mode both ways, pele variables mapped)
- `mock/server.ts`: Bun server on 9656 that ingests the fixture through core + analyzers and serves sessions, structure, graph, events, text (structural summarizer), digest, search, config, stream (fake `structure` event every 10 s), and the built `dist/`.

```
cd code && bun install
cd packages/ui
bun run mock      # fake engine on 127.0.0.1:9656 (also serves dist/ if built)
bun run dev       # Vite on 5173, proxies /api, /hook, /health to 9656
bun run build     # -> dist/ (index.html + assets, 401 kB JS / 140 kB gzip)
bun run typecheck
```

#!/bin/sh
# Forward the Claude Code hook JSON on stdin to the local yolo-twice engine. Never fails, never blocks.
PORT="${YOLO_TWICE_PORT:-9656}"
if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then

cat > bin/yolo-twice <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Run the yolo-twice engine CLI. Resolution order:
#   1. $YOLO_TWICE_ENGINE  (path to cli.js, or a command)
#   2. repo dev layout next to this plugin (code/packages/engine)
#   3. a marketplace clone under ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/*/code/packages/engine (built on first use with bun)
#   4. npx -y yolo-twice@latest
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
CMD="${1:-open}"; [ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
case "$CMD" in
  stop|status|index|start|open|mode|hook|help) ;;
  micro|attentive|balanced|yolo) set -- "$CMD" "$@"; CMD=mode ;;
  *) set -- "$CMD" "$@"; CMD=open ;;
esac

run_engine_dir() {
  dir="$1"; shift
  if [ -f "$dir/dist/cli.js" ]; then exec node "$dir/dist/cli.js" "$@"; fi
  if command -v bun >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$dir/src/cli.ts" ]; then
    if [ ! -d "$dir/../../node_modules" ]; then (cd "$dir/../.." && bun install >/dev/null 2>&1); fi
    exec bun run "$dir/src/cli.ts" "$@"
  fi
  return 1
}

if [ -n "${YOLO_TWICE_ENGINE:-}" ]; then
  case "$YOLO_TWICE_ENGINE" in
    *.js) exec node "$YOLO_TWICE_ENGINE" "$CMD" "$@" ;;
    *.ts) exec bun run "$YOLO_TWICE_ENGINE" "$CMD" "$@" ;;
    *) exec "$YOLO_TWICE_ENGINE" "$CMD" "$@" ;;
  esac
fi
if [ -d "$HERE/../packages/engine" ]; then run_engine_dir "$HERE/../packages/engine" "$CMD" "$@"; fi
for d in "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/marketplaces/*/code/packages/engine; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && run_engine_dir "$d" "$CMD" "$@"
done
exec npx -y yolo-twice@latest "$CMD" "$@"
EOF

Every committed file belongs to exactly one session, so teammates indexing in parallel never
   to the resumer's own paths, and runs `claude --resume <file> --fork-session`. The fork gets
   a new session id, so a committed session never gets a second writer and resuming a
   teammate's session cannot cause merge conflicts. Nothing is written into `~/.claude`.
7. Paths are portable and anonymous: the project root is written as `$PROJECT`, the home
   folder as `~`, Claude folder names derived from them as `<project-slug>` and `-~-`, other
   machines' homes as `~`, and the login name as `<user>`. This holds for every string of an
   event, including tool inputs and `data`. Switch it off with `redaction.paths: false`.
8. Redaction runs before anything is written: API keys, tokens, JWTs, private keys, env
   values and configurable patterns are replaced with `[redacted:<rule>]`; tool results above a
    meta.json                    # label, time span, event count, cost: what the project list needs
    events.ndjson                # redacted normalized events, append-only in arrival order
    structure.json               # L0 to L3 tree with available granularities per node
    graph.mmd, graph.L1.mmd      # flow graph as mermaid text, rendered with pele everywhere
    text/<node>.<gran>.<hash>.json   # summaries of finished nodes, keyed by input hash + analyzer version

    project.json                 # L-1 project list, rebuilt from every meta.json

Commit regularly: after each stable increment (a package with passing tests, a doc update), commit with a descriptive message. Don't wait for the whole task to finish. Leave in-progress parallel work (subagent directories) out of a commit until it reports back.

**Why:** Hackathon setting ([[yolo-twice-baselhack-context]]), four people pulling the repo; small commits keep teammates unblocked and make rollbacks cheap.

**How to apply:** Stage selectively with `git add <paths>`; commit without asking once a piece is verified; never push unless asked.

- **A fix along the way:** a pasted image used to become its own `[image]` prompt, which started a fake turn. It now stays with the prompt it came with. Claude Code's `[Image: source: /tmp/…]` note no longer shows up in labels.

- **Resume:** a resumed session gets its images back in the original prompts.
- **Privacy:** secret and path redaction can't see inside an image, so screenshots are committed as they are. `config.json` takes `"images": { "keep": false }` to turn this off, or `max_bytes` to cap the size (default 5 MB). Skipped images show a short note in the reader instead. The README and design doc say this.
- **Not included:** screenshots that tools take (for example during my browser checks) are not saved.

## 7. Coordinated views and deep links

The UI shows four linked views at once: a filter bar, a timeline scrubber, the reader (the
zoom tree) and the graph. They are projections of one state, and that state is the URL.

- **Focus narrows.** The focus is a node: the project, a session, a phase, a turn or a step.
  The reader is rooted at it, the graph is redrawn one level below it (semantic zoom, no pixel
  zoom), and the timeline axis spans it. A single click focuses (a graph node, a timeline bar, a session; in the reader the ⤢ button, since a row click expands), Esc goes up one level, the
  breadcrumb jumps anywhere above.
- **The window narrows in time.** Dragging on the timeline sets a window that snaps to whole
  bars (turns, or steps inside a turn), so it always maps to nodes in the tree and graph.
- **Filter and query highlight, they never hide.** Matches inside the focus show as ticks on
  the timeline, counts on reader rows and accented graph nodes; everything else is dimmed. An
  empty query with a filter lists every match, for example all your prompts. Query and filter
  combine with AND; filter codes combine with OR.
- **Selection and hover link.** Click selects a node in every view; hover highlights it in
  every view.
- **Follow.** Like `tail -f` or a CI log: the selection stays on the newest step, a focused
  turn moves to the newest turn, and the reader keeps the tail in view. Any navigation
|---|---|---|
| `project` | project folder name, `name~abcd` only when two projects share a name | the engine's last project |
| `session` | shortest unique session id prefix, at least 6 characters; a leading `~` means not pinned | project root |
| `focus` | structure node id such as `p2`, `t7`, `t1.s5` | the session |
| `t` | window in seconds from the focus start, snapped to whole bars | whole focus |
| `x` | selected node | none |
| `q` | text query | none |
| `k` | filters: `u` your prompts, `a` assistant text, `h` thinking, `t` tool calls, `t:Name` one tool, `e` tool errors, `s` subagents, `c` compactions and commands, `r` rewound turns | none |
| `z` | default text length: `t` title, `a` abstract, `s` summary, `f` full | `a` |
| `f` | follow: the view stays on the newest events as they arrive, like `tail -f` | off |

Example: `http://127.0.0.1:9656/yolo-twice/34b27c/t2?k=t,e&x=t2.s4`

Typing in the search box no longer loses keys, and the page freezes for much shorter moments. I reproduced both problems with a CPU slowed 4× and natural pauses between keys. "summarizer project split fails" came out as "sumaizrpojet sltfis", and each update blocked the page for up to 280 ms.

**Why keys were lost:** the box sends your text to the URL after a short pause. When the URL then updated, the box copied that older value back into itself and overwrote anything typed in between. Now it only takes the URL's value when it changes from elsewhere, such as the back button, a link or Clear.

**Why it froze:** every pause in typing re-ran the search, the dimming, the text view, the graph and the timeline, all at full priority. Now:
- Those views update at low priority, and React interrupts that work when you press the next key.
- Views whose inputs haven't changed skip re-rendering entirely.
- The box waits 200 ms after your last key instead of 150 ms.

**Result, same test:** the text arrives exactly as typed, and the longest freeze dropped from about 280 ms to about 120 ms at 4× slowdown, roughly 30 ms on a normal CPU. All 57 unit tests and the 30-check browser suite pass.

{"file_path":"~/.claude/plans/pasted-content-id-bba5-we-are-transient-nautilus.md","content":"# Reader: readable tool calls, search that opens to the passage, legend as filter

## Context

Three requests from using the revamped UI, plus one finished change that still needs its commit:

0. **Scroll lock (done, uncommitted).** Up locks follow in both panes, scrolling to the newest
   follows again, a floating "↓ N new" pill. The browser suite passes 11/11 after fixing the
   scroll-back-on-unlock loop (Zoom.tsx, Graph.tsx, App.tsx, Header.tsx, styles.css). Commit first.
1. **Tool calls are unreadable.** A Bash call shows as one JSON line with escaped newlines, often
   with a heredoc of Python inside. Analysis of 680 recorded calls: Bash 537 (`command`,
   `description`, `timeout`), Read 35 (`file_path`, `offset`, `limit`), Write 26 (`file_path`,
   `content`), WebFetch 15, WebSearch 9, MCP browser tools ~20, Agent 6, AskUserQuestion 5,
   Edit 2, ExitPlanMode 2. There is no schema in the transcript; shapes are stable per tool.
   About 30 inputs are not valid JSON any more because redaction truncates at 8000 chars.
2. **Search shows where, not what.** With `?q=input&k=u` the reader marks matching parts, but
   the matching passage stays hidden until you open each step and switch it to Raw.
3. **The graph legend should filter.** The legend lists the same kinds as the filter chips;
   clicking a kind should toggle that filter.

## 1. Tool calls as code (new `code/packages/ui/src/ToolCall.tsx`)

- Parse `tool.call` text as JSON; when it fails (truncated), recover the leading string fields
  with a tolerant scan and mark the card "cut off at 8000 characters".
- One renderer per common tool, a generic one for the rest:
  - **Bash:** `description` as the card title, `command` as shell code. A heredoc that feeds an
    interpreter (`python3 - <<'EOF'`, `node`, `bun`, `cat > file.ts <<EOF`) is split out and
    highlighted in its own language; the shell around it stays shell. `timeout`,
    `run_in_background` as small facts.
  - **Read / Write / Edit:** the path as a header (with line range for Read); Write content
    highlighted by file extension; Edit as a red/green diff of `old_string` → `new_string`.
  - **WebFetch / WebSearch:** URL or query as a link line, prompt as prose.
  - **Agent:** description as title, prompt as prose (serif). **AskUserQuestion:** the questions
    and options as a list. **ExitPlanMode:** the plan as prose.
  - **Anything else (MCP etc.):** a key/value list; long string values as code blocks, JSON
    values pretty-printed and highlighted.
- **Tool results:** Read results lose the `cat -n` line-number gutter into a real gutter and get
  highlighted by the file's extension (known from the paired call via `tool.call_id`); Bash
  output stays monospace; errors get the error tint.
- **Highlighter:** `highlight.js` core with only the languages that occur (bash, python,
  typescript/javascript, json, css, html/xml, diff, markdown, yaml): small, synchronous, no WASM.
  Token colours come from our palette (`--k-*`, ink), light and dark.
- Wire into `Events` in `Zoom.tsx` (replaces the `<pre>` for `tool.call` / `tool.result`).

## 2. Search opens to the passage (`Zoom.tsx`, `App.tsx`)

- Pass the scope's matching event ids to the reader. While a query or filter is active, steps
  that contain a match open automatically, at Raw detail (as a per-part setting, so the page
  switch shows "N parts at Raw" and the existing reset applies), with their ancestors open.
- Cap at 30 auto-opened steps; beyond that a line says "Showing the first 30 of N matching steps".
- Inside opened steps, matching events get a marker edge and the first match scrolls into view.
- **Highlight the words** in prose and code alike with the CSS Custom Highlight API
  (`CSS.highlights`): ranges over text nodes, so syntax-highlighted spans stay intact. Falls back
  to the existing `<mark>` in prose where the API is missing.
- Clearing the query closes what search opened (only the auto-opened parts).

## 3. Legend as filter (`Graph.tsx` `Legend`, `App.tsx`)

- Legend items become toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`, mapped to filter codes:
  You→`u`, Claude→`a`, Thinking→`h`, Tool→`t`, Error→`e`, Subagent→`s`,

- Active items get the chip "on" look; a tooltip says "Show only … (click again to clear)".

All four changes are in, each committed on its own, and none pushed. Your engine on port 9656 is running the new code, so a page reload shows everything.

1. **Follow mode scrolls like a terminal** (7d2753d):
   - Moving up in the text or the graph stops following, by wheel, keys, scrollbar or dragging.
   - Scrolling down to the newest content in either pane starts following again.
   - While following is off, a floating "↓ N new" button counts new events ("↓ Latest" when none have arrived) and jumps back when clicked.
   - I also fixed a loop where switching follow off made the panes scroll back to the newest node, which switched it on again. The graph would have pulled your view back the same way.

2. **Tool calls are readable** (93ff424). Claude Code stores no schema for tool inputs, but each tool's input has a stable shape across the 680 recorded calls, so each common tool gets its own layout:
   - **Bash:** the description is the title, and a heredoc inside the command is split out and highlighted as Python, JavaScript and so on. Your pasted example now shows as shell around highlighted Python.
   - **Read, Write and Edit:** the file path, the code highlighted by file extension, and Edit as a red/green diff.
   - **Web, agent and question tools:** prompts read as prose.
   - **Results:** Read output gets real line numbers, JSON is pretty-printed, and fenced code blocks are highlighted.
   - About 30 inputs were cut off when stored; they still show their beginning, with a note.

3. **Search opens to the passage** (dbdab43):
   - Steps with matches open at Raw (the first 30), the first match scrolls into view, and the words are highlighted inside code as well as prose.
   - Clearing the search closes only what it opened.
   - A filter on its own (for example Tools) also opens its matching steps, which can be a lot at once. In one turn, Tools opened 22 steps.

4. **The graph legend is a filter** (63e914f): clicking a kind toggles the same filter as its chip, and the two stay in sync through the URL.

Your example URL (`?q=input&k=u`) found nothing because the search treated `q=input&k=u&z=f` as a single word. Search now splits words at any non-letter character, so terms inside URLs and file names like `store.ts` are found. With that fixed, the URL opens your one matching prompt.
